processing.name: Dahanu–Gholvad–Valsad Coastal Agro-Industrial Corridor (MH & GJ)
products: Strategic Role: The pioneering and largest processing hub for value-added sapota in India. Houses farm-level solar drying sheds, cooperative women-led dehydration micro-enterprises, and industrial powder facilities.
catchment: Catchment: Dahanu, Gholvad, Bordi, Talasari (Palghar district, MH); Umbergaon, Pardi, Valsad, Bilimora, and Gandevi (Navsari district, GJ).

paragraphs.text: Strategic Role: The pioneering and largest processing hub for value-added sapota in India. Houses farm-level solar drying sheds, cooperative women-led dehydration micro-enterprises, and industrial powder facilities.
Key Entities: Dahanu Chikoo Processing Clusters, tribal SHG cooperatives supported by KVK Palghar, private freeze-drying units in Valsad/Vapi industrial estates, and artisanal wineries in Bordi.
Catchment: Dahanu, Gholvad, Bordi, Talasari (Palghar district, MH); Umbergaon, Pardi, Valsad, Bilimora, and Gandevi (Navsari district, GJ).

products: Strategic Role: Focused on bulk pulping, blast freezing, and cold-storage operations integrated into multi-fruit processing lines (switching from mango/guava to chiku).
catchment: Catchment: Ulavapadu, Kandukur (Prakasam); Dwarapudi (East Godavari); Periyakulam (Theni); and Palani foothills (Dindigul).

paragraphs.text: 3. South Indian Processing Nodes (Andhra Pradesh & Tamil Nadu)
Strategic Role: Focused on bulk pulping, blast freezing, and cold-storage operations integrated into multi-fruit processing lines (switching from mango/guava to chiku).
Key Facilities: Industrial units along the Chennai–Kolkata highway near Singarayakonda/Ongole (Prakasam), Chittoor fruit clusters, and fruit processing units around Theni/Dindigul.
Catchment: Ulavapadu, Kandukur (Prakasam); Dwarapudi (East Godavari); Periyakulam (Theni); and Palani foothills (Dindigul).

summary.text: India is the world's largest producer of sapota (commonly known as chikoo or chiku), contributing over 60% of global supply. Over the recent 3-year period (2021–22 to 2023–24), India’s total production has averaged between 800,000 and 860,000 metric tonnes (MT) annually, registering a combined 3-year production of approximately 2.45 to 2.60 million MT.

passages.text: Navsari & Valsad Belt (~52% – 58% of state output):
Remaining Districts (~6% – 10%): Bharuch, Anand, and Vadodara.
Remaining Districts (~18% – 24%): Nellore, Guntur, and Visakhapatnam.

Home to the Dahanu Gholvad Chikoo (GI). The calcium-rich maritime soil (weathered sea-shell alluvium) lends the fruit a distinct grainy texture and high sugar content (>11% TSS). Palghar serves as the prime supplier to Mumbai's APMC Vashi and direct air exports to the UK and Middle East
Northern Dry Zone (Belagavi, Bagalkote & Vijayapura) (~42% – 48% of state output):
Remaining Districts (~12% – 16%): Paschim Medinipur and Purba Bardhaman.
Remaining Districts (~28% – 34%): Virudhunagar, Salem, and Vellore.

Year-Round Staggered Harvesting: In tropical coastal belts (South Gujarat, Konkan, and Coastal AP), sapota flowers and fruits almost continuously. However, commercial harvest peaks in two distinct flushes: October to February (accounting for ~60% of total volume and highest market prices) and April to June (accounting for ~30%).

protection.name: Sapota Seed Borer / Fruit Borer (Trymalitis margarita)
protection.geography: All-India Commercial Belts (Heavy in Gujarat, MH, Karnataka, AP)
protection.impact: Tiny caterpillar bores into young marble-sized fruit, tunnels through pulp, and feeds directly on developing seeds; entry hole plugged with dark granular frass; causes premature fruit ripening, hardening, and fruit drop.
protection.passage: Sapota — source table 3, row 2: All-India Commercial Belts (Heavy in Gujarat, MH, Karnataka, AP) / Sapota Seed Borer / Fruit Borer (Trymalitis margarita). Management modes extracted without formulations, rates, schedules or PHIs.

protection.name: Leaf Webber / Shoot Borer (Nephopteryx eugraphella)
protection.geography: High-Humidity Coastal Belts (Navsari, Valsad, Palghar, Konkan)
protection.impact: Larvae web leaves, terminal shoots, and flower buds together into dense silken clusters filled with chewed leaf scraps and excreta; feed on chlorophyll inside webs; buds wither, leading to skeletonized shoots.
protection.passage: Sapota — source table 3, row 3: High-Humidity Coastal Belts (Navsari, Valsad, Palghar, Konkan) / Leaf Webber / Shoot Borer (Nephopteryx eugraphella). Management modes extracted without formulations, rates, schedules or PHIs.

protection.name: Leaf Spot & Fruit Spot (Phaeophleospora indica / Cercospora zapotae)
protection.geography: Humid Maritime & Monsoon Tracts (South Gujarat, Konkan, Coastal AP)
protection.impact: Small, circular, reddish-brown spots with dark purple borders and pale white centers on leaves; coalescing lesions cause yellowing and severe premature defoliation; superficial spots on fruit ruin table quality.
protection.passage: Sapota — source table 3, row 4: Humid Maritime & Monsoon Tracts (South Gujarat, Konkan, Coastal AP) / Leaf Spot & Fruit Spot (Phaeophleospora indica / Cercospora zapotae). Management modes extracted without formulations, rates, schedules or PHIs.

protection.name: Sooty Mold (Capnodium spp.)
protection.geography: Humid & Shaded Orchards (WB, Konkan, Coastal AP)
protection.impact: Thick, black, velvety superficial fungal mat covering leaves, twigs, and fruit; blocks sunlight and impairs photosynthesis, causing fruit to remain stunted, small, and unmarketable.
protection.passage: Sapota — source table 3, row 5: Humid & Shaded Orchards (WB, Konkan, Coastal AP) / Sooty Mold (Capnodium spp.). Management modes extracted without formulations, rates, schedules or PHIs.

protection.name: Green Scale & Mealybugs (Coccus viridis, Phenacoccus spp.)
protection.geography: Peninsular Drylands & Coastal Belts (AP, Karnataka, TN, MH)
protection.impact: Green oval soft scales and white mealybugs cluster along leaf midribs, tender shoots, and fruit pedicels; suck sap, excrete honeydew that fuels sooty mold, and stunt fruit sizing.
protection.passage: Sapota — source table 3, row 6: Peninsular Drylands & Coastal Belts (AP, Karnataka, TN, MH) / Green Scale & Mealybugs (Coccus viridis, Phenacoccus spp.). Management modes extracted without formulations, rates, schedules or PHIs.

protection.name: Stem End Rot & Soft Rot (Botryodiplodia theobromae / Phomopsis spp.)
protection.impact: Dark brown discoloration initiating at the fruit stem scar during ripening; spreads down through the soft pulp, resulting in a watery, foul-smelling black rot within 48 hours.
protection.passage: Sapota — source table 3, row 7: Post-Harvest Supply Chain & Exports / Stem End Rot & Soft Rot (Botryodiplodia theobromae / Phomopsis spp.). Management modes extracted without formulations, rates, schedules or PHIs.

context: State-Wise & Variety-Wise Market Availability Calendar

Because sapota (Manilkara zapota L. van Royen, syn. Achras zapota L.) is an evergreen tropical tree grown largely in maritime and warm semi-arid belts, it exhibits near-continuous flowering and fruiting throughout the year. However, commercial harvests peak in two distinct flushes: the primary winter flush (accounting for ~60% of annual volume, commanding top table prices due to slow sugar accumulation) and the secondary summer flush (~30% of volume).
Key Table Varieties & Belts (Domestic & Export Footprint)

Fresh sapota exports from India average 3,000 to 5,500 MT annually. Growth is heavily driven by Dahanu Gholvad (GI) from Maharashtra and Kalipatti from South Gujarat, shipped by air cargo and short-sea reefers under modified atmosphere packaging (MAP).
Key Processed Products & Production Breakdown Estimates
Commercial processing absorbs approximately 2.5% to 4.0% of India's gross sapota harvest (roughly 20,000 to 35,000 MT of fresh fruit equivalents annually).

Processing is constrained by biochemical instability: sapota pulp contains active polyphenol oxidases (PPO) and leucoanthocyanidins (tannins) which cause rapid enzymatic browning, astringency reversion, and off-flavor development during thermal pasteurization. Modern processing heavily leverages dehydration, low-temperature vacuum evaporation, and freeze-drying.

Dehydrated Sapota Slices & Solar Chikoo Chips: Thinly sliced mature-ripe peeled chiku treated with mild potassium metabisulfite (KMS) or citric acid solutions and dried in solar-tunnel or heat-pump dryers (moisture <10%); eaten as crunchy fruit chips or rehydrated for milkshakes.

Freeze-Dried & Spray-Dried Sapota Powder: Vacuum freeze-dried () or spray-dried pulp powder using maltodextrin as an encapsulation carrier; core raw material for instant milkshake mixes, infant food formulations, confectionery, and dairy ice cream bases.

Aseptic & Frozen Sapota Pulp/Puree (20° to 22° Brix): Cold-pulped, de-seeded, enzyme-deactivated (via flash thermal inactivation at 85–90°C with ascorbic acid adjustment to pH <4.2), and blast-frozen or packed in aseptic bag-in-drum formats for commercial ice cream and beverage compounding (e.g., Naturals Ice Cream).
Chikoo Halwa, Jams & Fruit Spreads: Traditional high-sugar preserves where natural pectin and sugar balance fruit solids without distinct enzymatic discoloration.

Chikoo Wine & Fermented Spirits: Niche artisanal alcoholic beverages (10–12% ABV) and fermented vinegars produced in the Dahanu-Bordi belt, capitalizing on the high natural sugar content of the fruit.

1. Dahanu–Gholvad–Valsad Coastal Agro-Industrial Corridor (MH & GJ)

Strategic Role: The pioneering and largest processing hub for value-added sapota in India. Houses farm-level solar drying sheds, cooperative women-led dehydration micro-enterprises, and industrial powder facilities.
Key Entities: Dahanu Chikoo Processing Clusters, tribal SHG cooperatives supported by KVK Palghar, private freeze-drying units in Valsad/Vapi industrial estates, and artisanal wineries in Bordi.
Catchment: Dahanu, Gholvad, Bordi, Talasari (Palghar district, MH); Umbergaon, Pardi, Valsad, Bilimora, and Gandevi (Navsari district, GJ).
2. Central Gujarat Industrial Corridor (Anand, Vadodara & Surat)
Strategic Role: Concentrated on commercial dairy inclusions, aseptic purees, and fruit paste manufacturing for pan-Indian ice cream and confectionery manufacturers.
Primary Facilities: Multi-fruit processing lines and contract dehydrators.
Catchment: Commercial arrivals from Gandevi/Navsari, Surat rural, and Bharuch canal tracts.
3. South Indian Processing Nodes (Andhra Pradesh & Tamil Nadu)
Strategic Role: Focused on bulk pulping, blast freezing, and cold-storage operations integrated into multi-fruit processing lines (switching from mango/guava to chiku).
Key Facilities: Industrial units along the Chennai–Kolkata highway near Singarayakonda/Ongole (Prakasam), Chittoor fruit clusters, and fruit processing units around Theni/Dindigul.
Catchment: Ulavapadu, Kandukur (Prakasam); Dwarapudi (East Godavari); Periyakulam (Theni); and Palani foothills (Dindigul).
Crop Phenology & Climatic Parameters

Sapota (Manilkara zapota) is an evergreen, slow-growing tree well adapted to tropical maritime climates. It tolerates high winds, atmospheric salinity, and shallow soils, but is susceptible to severe frost. The physiological cycle from floral bud break to harvest maturity is unusually protracted, taking 240 to 300 days (8 to 10 months).

Detailed Phenological Breakdown
Floral Initiation & Anthesis (Day 0 – 35)
Phenology: Solitary flowers emerge in the leaf axils on terminal shoots. Flowers are small, bisexual, campanulate, and white.

Flowering Behavior: Exhibits protogyny (the stigma becomes receptive 12–24 hours before the anthers dehisce and shed pollen), which promotes cross-pollination. Entomophilous pollination is conducted primarily by honeybees (Apis spp.), thrips, and wind.
Ideal Climate: 25–32°C; relative humidity >60–70%. Extreme dry heat (>41°C) with low humidity dries out stigmatic surfaces, causing heavy flower drop.
Fruit Set & Pea Stage (Day 36 – 60)
Phenology: Petals and stamens wither; ovary swells into a small green berrylet covered with dense brown scurfy pubescence.
Abscission Dynamics: High natural abscission occurs; less than 10–12% of total flowers set fruit, and only 1–3% of initial fruitlets reach commercial maturity.
Irrigation: Soil moisture must remain consistent; alternating dry and wet cycles triggers fruitlet shedding.
Cell Division & Marble Stage (Day 61 – 150)
Phenology: Rapid cell division in the mesocarp; seed primordia form; fruit expands to marble size (15–25 mm).

Physiological Trait: The developing fruit is packed with branched laticifers containing abundant, sticky white latex (chicle) and high concentrations of astringent soluble polyphenols (leucoanthocyanidins/tannins) that act as natural chemical defenses against pests.
Fruit Bulking & Sizing Phase (Day 151 – 240)
Phenology: Cell division halts entirely; fruit expands via continuous cell enlargement; inner seed coats turn dark brown to black and harden.
Ideal Climate: Warm, humid maritime conditions (26–34°C).

Agronomic Management: High potassium () fertigation demand; foliar application of Sulfate of Potash (00:00:50 @ 1.0%) + Gibberellic Acid ( @ 25–50 ppm) improves fruit expansion and reduces premature drop.
Physiological Maturity & Ripening Window (Day 241 – 280+)

Phenology: Fruit reaches maximum size; brown scaly scurf (scurfiness) on the skin rubs off easily, exposing a pale yellowish/light brown smooth epidermis; internal latex disappears (a scratch reveals a yellow/green streak rather than white milky latex); stylar crown/remains at the apex drop off cleanly.

Harvest Calibration: Because sapota is climacteric, it must be harvested at full physiological maturity (when TSS reaches 12–14° Brix on the tree) but while the fruit remains rock-firm. Post-harvest ripening at ambient conditions (24–28°C) takes 4 to 7 days, during which starch converts to sugars (TSS hits 18–24° Brix) and insoluble tannins condense, eliminating astringency.
Phytosanitary Matrix: Major Pests, Diseases & Management
Sapota is a resilient evergreen tree, but high-density commercial orchards face severe losses from lepidopteran borers and foliar fungal blights during warm, humid monsoon spells.
